prior_importants.description: An `adr-number` refusal is reported as a flagged-debt refusal. The CLI prints "Merge refused:  flagged. Re-run with --accept-debt …" and the `pup status` inbox / conductor show "gate refused on flagged debt" with an `--accept-debt` command. Neither fixes the clash, because the ADR stage runs before debt is measured.

findings.description: A PR closed on GitHub without merging is counted as an open PR forever. Its numbers stay taken permanently. If its gated sha is ever pruned, every ADR-adding gate in the repo fails, and nothing in the store can retire the PR.
findings.body:
**A PR closed without merging is counted as an open PR forever, and nothing in the store can retire it.**

`competingBranches` decides a merged session's PR is open from the store alone: any `merged` session whose `newestMerge` is a merge event with a `prUrl` (no `landed` event after it) becomes an open-PR peer read at its pinned sha.

```ts
const merge = session.state === 'merged' ? newestMerge(db, session.id) : undefined;
if (typeof merge !== 'object' || merge.prUrl === undefined) continue;
const rev = COMMIT_SHA.test(String(merge.sha)) ? merge.sha : undefined;
competitors.push({ branch: session.branch, rev, prUrl: merge.prUrl });
```

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/a31ea13e70035f21915833ac72facc77045d2eb3/src/core/adr-number.service.ts#L205-L208>

Nothing retires such a session if its PR is closed rather than merged:
- `landed` is written only by `pup land` (`land.service.ts:213`), after it refuses any PR whose state is not `MERGED` (`land.service.ts:114`).
- `merged` is terminal (`TRANSITIONS.merged` is `[]`, `session-state.utils.ts:18`), so `pup kill` throws `InvalidTransitionError`.
- `pup fix` and re-gate both refuse a closed PR (`fix-round.service.ts:606-617`, `regate.service.ts:106-116`).
- No code deletes a session row, and nothing in the gate asks GitHub whether the PR is still open.

**Trigger:** a session's PR adds `docs/adr/0150-x.md` and is closed without merging, for example because the work is redone in a new session.
1. **Permanent number squatting.** Up to three decision numbers stay taken in every later gate. A session that reuses 0150 for the redone decision is refused as "also added by pup/…, a session branch that is live or has an open PR", which is untrue. The only way out is to renumber or edit the store by hand.
2. **Repo-wide refusal after a prune.** If the closed PR's remote branch is deleted, then pruned and gc'd past the prune window, the pinned commit leaves the repo. Lines 294-306 and 383 then refuse every gate that adds a decision until someone fetches the PR head again. The block comes back after every prune.

ADR 0146 defines peers as sessions "`merged` with an open PR that has not landed" and accepts the unreadable-commit block only "until its PR lands or its head is fetched". A closed PR never lands, and the ADR does not mention closed PRs.

**Possible fixes:**
- Have `pup land`, or another path, record a terminal event for a `CLOSED` PR that `newestMerge` treats like `landed`.
- Or add an operator command to retire it.
- At minimum, ADR 0146 should name this as a ceiling.

findings.description: The free-number suggestion can hand out the number of one of the branch's own misnamed files. `taken` is built only from `onTarget`, `takenBy` and `added`, so a misnamed path's intended number is never in it. Example: the target ends at 0146, and a branch adds `docs/adr/0146-y.md` plus `docs/adr/0147-x.MD`. The stage says to rewrite the second as `docs/adr/0147-x.md` and also to renumber the first to 0147. A worker that does both is refused next round as a duplicate. Fix: add `decisionNumber(meantAs(path))` to `taken` for each misnamed path before the first `renumber()`.

The case-blind listing `:(top,literal,icase)docs/adr/` folds ASCII only, because git's icase pathspec compares byte by byte. A branch that adds `docſ/adr/0146-x.md` (U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S in place of `s`) is therefore listed neither as a decision nor as misnamed, and the stage passes even when 0146 is taken. If a case-insensitive macOS filesystem folds U+017F to `s` (not verified), a checkout there puts two 0146 decisions in one `docs/adr/` folder. That is the exposure the misnamed refusal exists to close. The session has to pick this spelling on purpose, and the scope audit still applies.

"A branch that adds no decision never reaches this check, so such a peer blocks only ADR-adding gates" is ambiguous. "A branch" means the gated branch and "such a peer" means the competing PR whose commit cannot be read, but a reader can take it to mean that a peer adding no decision is skipped. Suggested wording: "The unreadable-PR refusal comes after the early return for a gated branch that adds no decision, so such a peer blocks only gates that add an ADR."

The comment "Everything else the case-blind listing found, but the index." calls README.md "the index". The code excludes `ADR_README`, and the uncommitted ADR index from decision 133 is a different file, so a reader may think the stage excludes that index. Reword it to "bar README.md", or delete it, since `ADR_README` already says so.

The new CLI refusal branches on `failedStage.stage === ADR_NUMBER_STAGE` only to swap "renumber its ADR as the report says" for "fix it". The dashboard branch this PR adds uses one generic message for every failed stage, and the CLI could do the same. Dropping the ternary removes the CLI's only import from the ADR module and one test branch, and the gate report already says to renumber.

The comment "accepting debt cannot get it through, only the session's own fix can" repeats the message printed right below it ("which --accept-debt does not cover. Steer the session to fix it"). The dashboard comment and a test comment make the same claim again. The only thing the message does not carry is "refused before any debt was weighed (decision 146)". Shorten the comment to that.

The end of the 25-line `adrNumberStage` JSDoc describes read mechanics (pinned shas through `runGit`, never a worktree, branches resolved one at a time). ADR 0146's Reads section, `competingBranches` and `decisionPaths` already document this. The ragged fragments left by successive rewrites make the docstring hard to scan. Trim it to the stage's outcomes and point to decision 146 for how it reads.

`numbersOf` (with its `as number` cast), `isOverrun` and `OVERRUN_CODES` each have a single caller. Inlining them as `new Set(targetPaths.map(...))` at line 276, and as `['ETIMEDOUT','ENOBUFS'].includes(code)` in `peerDecisions`'s catch with the doc comment kept as a WHY there, removes two functions and a constant with no change in behaviour.

process_issues.description: Skipped review-context (no CI/infra/protocol surface), review-workflow-safety (no .github/workflows change), review-maintainability (off the default roster at standard depth) and review-spec (the PR closes no issue and no --spec was given; the PR body's acceptance list is not an issue). Correctness and security ran two instances each: 428 source lines plus 675 test lines is past the size gate. Correctness was split into adr-number.service.ts logic and the gate/CLI/dashboard integration; security into git argv/config evasion and output/resource bounds.

The integration instance noted, without reporting them as findings, four JSDocs that still describe a gate refusal as flagged debt only: `gateRefused` in src/core/types/dashboard.types.ts ~L163-167, `needsYou` in dashboard.service.ts L410-412, and `refuseGate` and `runMergeGate` in merge-gate.service.ts (L2950, L1052-1067). They are not recorded.
The git-surface instance's `bash scripts/adr-index.sh` needed approval under the CI lock. It read ADRs 0146 and 0101 directly instead, with no loss of coverage.
